title: Decision problems and finite descriptions

based_on.title: Formalizing Computability Theory via Partial Recursive Functions
based_on.venue: 10th International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP 2019)

summary: Express yes-or-no questions as sets of natural numbers, encode finite descriptions, and prove that no numbered family of programs can decide every numerical problem.
abstract: An evenness test answers one question for every natural-number input. A table of answers for the first thousand numbers answers only finitely many instances. To study this distinction, we represent a yes-or-no problem by the set of inputs whose answer is yes, and distinguish its mathematical answer function from a procedure that produces those answers. Finite strings of instructions can be assigned distinct natural-number codes. Once programs are numbered, a diagonal argument constructs a problem that none of them decides: any proposed program fails when tested on its own number. This obstruction uses only the numbering and the meaning assigned to each program; it does not depend on choosing a particular programming language.
